title: Introduction to Python
description: What Python is and how to make the computer show a message on the screen.

items.sub: You write instructions. The computer follows them.
Python runs your lines top to bottom, in order.
Words like `print`, `if` and `for`, not secret symbols.
Games, websites, robots, science and AI.

content.text: A recipe is a list of steps in order. A program is too. The computer is the cook: it follows every step exactly as written, and never guesses what you meant.

steps.label: You write code
steps.detail: Lines of instructions in the editor.

steps.label: Python reads it
steps.detail: One line at a time, from the top.

content.title: From your code to the screen

content.question: In what order does Python run your instructions?
options: Top to bottom, one line at a time
All lines at the same moment
content.explain: Python starts at the first line and works down, one line at a time. That is why the order you write things in matters.

items: `print` tells the computer: show this on the screen.
The parentheses `()` hold whatever you want to show.
Text goes inside quotation marks: `"like this"`.
Every `print` puts its message on a new line.
content.title: How print works

parts.label: command
parts.note: The instruction name. It means: show something on the screen.

parts.label: open
parts.note: Opens the box of things you hand to `print`.

parts.label: message
parts.note: The text to show. The quotes tell Python this is text, and they do not appear in the output.

parts.label: close
parts.note: Closes the box. Every `(` needs a matching `)`.

content.code:
print("Hello, World!")
print("I am learning Python!")

steps.note: Python reads line 1. It is a `print`, so the message inside the quotes appears in the output.
Line 2 is another `print`. Its message goes on a new line, below the first one.

content.title: Watch it run, line by line
content.outro: Two print lines, two lines of output, in the same order. Press **Try it** to run it yourself.

items.title: Works
items.text: The quotes tell Python that `Hi` is text to show.

items.title: Error
items.text: No quotes, so Python looks for something named `Hi`, finds nothing, and stops with a `NameError`.

content.question: Which line shows the word Pizza on the screen?
content.explain: The command comes first, then parentheses, and the text goes inside quotes: `print("Pizza")`.

practice.question: Use print to make the computer show your name.

quiz.question: What does `print` do?
options: It prints paper from a printer.
It shows text on the screen.
quiz.explain: `print` shows text or numbers on the screen. It has nothing to do with a paper printer.
